newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Issing says German repo cut sent clear signal.
newsitem.headline: Issing says German repo cut sent clear signal.

text.p: Otmar Issing, the Bundesbank chief economist, said the German central bank's latest repo rate cut on August 22 sent a clear signal to the markets.
Noting that the cut to 3.00 percent from 3.30 percent was "clearly more than many had expected", he said the current repo rate had now reached an "all-time low".

Reiterating comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, Issing told a financial seminar in Zurich that he once more wanted to make clear that the Bundesbank had sent a signal with its larger-than-expected cut.
"We have created clarity for the foreseeable future," he said, echoing views Tietmeyer's had expressed.
"With this clear step we are signalling that the level has been reached."
He said slowing money supply growth allowed the Bundesbank to take this step.
He added that addressing Germany's unemployment problem and reforming its tax system was now in the hands of politicians in Bonn, not something for the Bundesbank.
